MFA No.4660/2020 is filed by the claimants, whereas MFA No.3659/2020 is filed by the KSRTC (for short, 'the Corporation') under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, (for short, 'the Act')
being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 21.01.2020 passed by the Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru City (for short, 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.1711/2019.

sentences.text:
Since the challenge is to the same judgment, both the appeals are clubbed together, heard and common judgment is being passed.
2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeals briefly stated are that on 03.02.2019 at about 6.30 a.m. the deceased Nithish Gowda was proceeding from Aradeshahalli bus stand towards Jalige.

When he reached near Aradeshahalli gate, Bengaluru-Doddaballapura main road, at that time, a KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-40/F-1300 which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the deceased.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained NC: 2023:KHC:40607 grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries at the hospital.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
4. On service of summons, the respondent appeared through counsel and filed written statement in which the averments made in the petition were denied.
The age, occupation and income of the deceased are denied.
It was pleaded that the petition itself is false and frivolous in the eye of law.
It was further pleaded that the accident was due to negligence of the deceased himself.
It was further pleaded that the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimants, in order to prove their case, examined claimant No.1 as PW-1 and got exhibited NC: 2023:KHC:40607 documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.
On behalf of respondent, one witness was examined as RW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R13.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia

, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver at 85% and negligence of the deceased at 15%, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.4,52,500/- along with interest at the rate of 7% p.a. and directed the Corporation to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, these appeals have been filed.
6. The learned counsel for the Corporation has raised the following contentions:
(i) Firstly, the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased himself.

The Tribunal has erred in holding that the driver of the bus has contributed 85% NC:
2023:KHC:40607 to the accident.

It is very clear from the sketch and evidence of the parties that the accident occurred at the middle of the road, the deceased while taking Anitha M vs The Chairman And Managing Director on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8269928/
4 U-turn, entered the main road without observing traffic.

(ii) Secondly, the driver of the bus has been examined as RW1.
He has categorically stated that the deceased turned his motorcycle towards Adarasanahalli without observing the traffic rules and he came in the middle of the road.
He further deposed that he has also lodged a complaint against the deceased but the police have refused to register the complaint.
He further deposed that, in fact, police have registered FIR against the father of the deceased under Sections 279, 304-A of IPC.
At the time of the accident the deceased was a minor and he was not having any driving licence, due to his negligence the accident has occurred.

Therefore, the finding of the NC:
2023:KHC:40607 Tribunal that the driver of the KSRTC bus has contributed 85% to the accident is contrary to the materials available on record.
(iii) Thirdly, at the time of the accident the deceased was a minor, the claimants have not produced any document to show that he was earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly relied on the judgment of the Apex court in the case of KISHAN GOPAL & ANOTHER vs. LALA & OTHERS reported in 2014 (1) SCC 244.

The case of the claimants is that, on 03.02.2019 at about 6.30 a.m. the deceased Nithish Gowda was proceeding from Aradeshahalli bus stand towards Jalige.

When he reached near Aradeshahalli gate, Bengaluru- Doddaballapura main road, at that time, a KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-40/F-1300, which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the deceased.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries at the hospital.
10. To prove their case, claimant No.1 was examined as PW1.
She has reiterated the averments made in the claim petition.

In the cross-examination, she has denied that, her son, while taking U-turn,
without observing the vehicle movements, rode the motorcycle at a high speed - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:40607 and in a rash and negligent manner.
She admitted that her son was about to come by taking U-turn in the place of the accident.
PW1 is not an eyewitness to the accident.
To prove her contention, she has produced Exs. P1 to P12.
Respondent examined the driver of the KSRTC bus as RW1.

He has reiterated the statement made in the written statement and contended Anitha M vs The Chairman And Managing Director on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8269928/

He further deposed that the deceased was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, without observing the traffic rules, took U-turn and entered intro the main road and accident has occurred.
Immediately he reported the same to the higher authorities of the Corporation and also ready to file a complaint to the police authority.
Respondent has produced Exs. R1 to R13 to support the case.
In the cross-examination of RW1, nothing worthwhile has been elicited.
11. Ex.P1 is the FIR which discloses that the complaint has been lodged by eyewitness to the accident - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:40607 by name Pattabhirama.
He has not been examined by either of the parties.
As per the complaint, when he was drinking tea at Aradeshanahalli gate on 03.02.2019 at about 6.30 a.m. the deceased was riding the motorcycle.
When he was trying to take U-turn, at that time KSRTC bus came from Bangalore in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result, he fell down from the motorcycle and suffered grievous injuries.
The police have registered FIR in Crime No.0007/2019 for offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304A of IPC.
AS per Ex.P10 - spot mahazar it reveals that accident occurred in the middle of the road.
At the time of the accident, the deceased has turned his motorcycle towards Aradeshanahalli gate.
At that time, the bus coming from Bangalore dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
It appears that deceased also contributed some percentage of negligence to the accident.
If the deceased, by observing oncoming vehicle movements turned his motorcycle, this accident would not have taken place.
At the same time, the driver of the bus - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:40607 also should have taken more care where the bus was coming in the junction.
Therefore, it appears that both the deceased as well as driver of the offending vehicle have contributed to the accident.
The parties have not produced IMV report of the motorcycle and the offending bus.

Considering the evidence of PW1 and RW1 and considering Exs.P1 - FIR, P10 - spot mahazar, P11 - charge sheet, I am of the opinion that the deceased has contributed 25% to the accident and the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-40/F-1300 contributed 75% to the accident.

At the time of the accident the claimant was aged 17 years 362 days.

In this regard, this Court in the case of CHETANA (supra) has held as follows:

Admittedly, the deceased was aged 17 years as on the date of the accident.
He might not be an adult but he cannot be considered as a child.

He has to be considered as an - 15 - Anitha M vs The Chairman And Managing Director on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8269928/

Section 2 (i) and (ii) of the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (for short "the Act") defines as follows:
"(i) "adolescent" means a person who has completed his fourteenth year of age but has not completed his eighteenth year;
"(ii) "child" means a person who has not completed his fourteenth year of age or such age as may be specified in the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (35 of 2009), whichever is more."
11. Section 3 of the Act prohibits employment of a child in certain occupations and processes. The said Act does not prohibit the adolescent of 17 years to involve in a milk vending business.

sentences.text: The deceased and his family are from rural area and it is common for a person of 17 years to be involved in milk vending or similar occupations.
The Tribunal has completely lost sight of this fact and the reasoning is contrary to and in the teeth of the statutory provisions."
In view of the above, the judgment relied upon by the Tribunal on KISHAN GOPAL (supra) is not applicable to the facts of this case.
13. The claimants claim that deceased was earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
But they have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2019, the notional income of the deceased has to be taken at Rs.14,000/- p.m.
Considering the evidence of PW1 and the materials available on record the monthly income has to be considered as Rs.12,000/-.
To the aforesaid income, 40% has to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in 'PRANAY SETHI' (supra).
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.16,800/-.

Since the deceased was a bachelor, 50% of the income has to be - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:40607 deducted towards personal expenses and remaining amount, i.e., Rs.8,400/-
has to be taken as his contribution to the family.
The multiplier applicable to his age group is '18'.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.18,14,400/- (Rs.8,400*12*18) on account of 'loss of dependency'.
14.
In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.

In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of 'MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE' (supra), claimant Nos.1 and 2, parents of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of filial consortium'.

In the result, I pass the following order:
(i) The appeals are disposed of.
(ii) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
The claimants are entitled to 75% of the total compensation of Rs.19,24,400/, i.e., Rs.14,43,300/- as against Rs.4,52,500/- awarded by the Tribunal.
